findings.reason: The protected sources always allocate the rolling DP line by the original column count and therefore use O(n) space on an m-by-n matrix, including wide one-row inputs. The candidate traverses columns as logical lines only when the matrix is wider than tall, reducing auxiliary space to O(min(m,n)) without changing O(mn) time.

The square-side recurrence is invariant under transposition. The candidate uses zip(*matrix) as a lazy logical transpose, retaining only one O(min(m,n))-sized tuple and DP line rather than materializing a second matrix; wide, square, and tall benchmark shapes all pass.

The legal 8/64/256-cell all-one tiers bind size to mn and exercise every DP update across wide, square, and tall shapes. The candidate passes at -0.01 relative exponent; a correct implementation that enumerates and validates every candidate square passes all outputs and fails only scaling (+0.91 relative exponent; 30.51x largest runtime ratio).
